DEFINE.core_strategy: Let the user explicitly choose standard input as the text source. Stdin text flows through the same single decode and counting path as a file, so counts, output shape and error contracts stay identical. Only the error text names <stdin> instead of a path.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Read standard input implicitly when no argument is given, as wc does.
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: It breaks the kept contract that no argument is a usage error with exit status 2.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Detect piped input automatically and read it when present.
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: Behavior would depend on the calling environment. It is harder to test and conflicts with the no-argument usage error.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Add a separate command or entry point dedicated to standard input.
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: It duplicates the output and error contracts in two places, so they can drift apart.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Give stdin its own read, decode and error path beside the file path.
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: The rules and messages could diverge between sources. The architecture already forbids a second decoding path for counting.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Copy standard input to a temporary file and reuse the file path unchanged.
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: It adds filesystem writes and cleanup. Error messages would name a temporary path instead of <stdin>.

dependencies.description: An architecture update that moves stdin processing and the '-' argument out of the hello system and hello-cli 'Does NOT own' lists.
The existing word, character and line counters, unchanged, reused for stdin text.
The four Quality Gate commands recorded in AGENTS.md.

assumptions.description: Users accept an explicit '-' argument for stdin, as in common Unix tools.
assumptions.how_checked: Review the README usage section and the feature request in DG-0004 against the delivered behavior.
assumptions.if_false: Re-open DISCOVER on how users expect to invoke stdin counting.

assumptions.description: Stdin text decoded as UTF-8 gives the same counts as the same bytes in a file.
assumptions.how_checked: Feed identical byte sequences, including CRLF and non-ASCII samples, by file and by stdin and compare output lines.
assumptions.if_false: Treat it as a defect in the shared decode path before release.

assumptions.description: Users rarely need to count a file literally named '-' by that bare name.
assumptions.how_checked: Document the './-' workaround in the README and watch for reports.
assumptions.if_false: Revisit the stdin marker choice in a later strategy.

risks.description: Stdin decoding could differ from file decoding, for example through newline translation.
risks.impact: CR and CRLF line counts could differ between stdin and file input.
risks.mitigation: Require byte-level equivalence tests for CR, CRLF and LF between both sources.

risks.description: Reading stdin could raise an unexpected error case.
risks.impact: A traceback could reach stderr, breaking the single-line error contract.
risks.mitigation: Cover stdin error cases in the no-traceback acceptance tests.

risks.description: Argument handling changes could alter the no-argument or many-argument behavior.
risks.impact: The exit status 2 usage contract could break.
risks.mitigation: Keep the existing usage-error regression tests and add a case for '-' with a second argument.

risks.description: An interactive terminal on stdin waits for end of input.
risks.impact: A user could think the command hangs.
risks.mitigation: State in the README that '-' reads until end of input.

DEFINE.thesis: Let wordcount count piped text through an explicit '-' argument now, closing a gap deferred across three strategies without changing any existing contract.

goals.description: Users can count text piped into wordcount without writing a temporary file.
goals.why: Pipeline use is the core gap DG-0004 names.
goals.success_metric: 'printf "a b\n" | wordcount -' prints 'words: 2 characters: 2 lines: 1' and exits 0.

goals.description: Stdin and file input give identical counts for identical bytes.
goals.why: The word, character and line rules must not depend on the source.
goals.success_metric: Every equivalence test sample gives the same output line from both sources.

goals.description: Invalid UTF-8 on stdin fails like a file error and names <stdin>.
goals.why: Users need the same clear, single-line error contract for both sources.
goals.success_metric: Exit status 1, one stderr line naming <stdin>, empty stdout, no traceback.

success_criteria.measurement: Acceptance tests in tests/features and tests/test_cli.py
success_criteria.target: All stdin scenarios pass, including empty stdin printing 'words: 0 characters: 0 lines: 0'
success_criteria.baseline: No stdin support, '-' is treated as a file path

success_criteria.measurement: Tests comparing file and stdin output for the same bytes

success_criteria.target: All pass unchanged, including exit status 2 with no argument

non_goals.description: Counting several inputs in one invocation or printing totals.
non_goals.tradeoff: It keeps the single-input, single-line output contract unchanged.

non_goals.description: Non-UTF-8 encodings or encoding options for stdin.
non_goals.tradeoff: It keeps one decoding rule for every source.

non_goals.description: Reading stdin when no argument is given.
non_goals.tradeoff: It keeps the exit status 2 usage contract the handoff requires.

non_goals.description: New output fields or a different output shape for stdin.
non_goals.tradeoff: It keeps one output line for every source, so scripts need no special case.

in_scope: Explicit '-' argument selects standard input as the text source
Stdin text counted with the existing word, character and line rules
Same three-field output line for stdin
Invalid UTF-8 on stdin: exit 1, one stderr line naming <stdin>
README and acceptance test updates for stdin
Architecture ownership update for stdin input
out_of_scope: Changes to the word, character or line rules
Changes to file-path error messages or exit statuses
Word, character and line counting, which already exist

walkthrough.name: Counting piped text
today: wordcount treats '-' as a file path.
It prints 'wordcount: error: file not found: -' and exits 1.
with_strategy: wordcount reads and decodes standard input once.
It prints 'words: <N> characters: <M> lines: <L>' and exits 0, the same as 'wordcount notes.txt'.

walkthrough.name: Invalid bytes on stdin
today: wordcount reports file not found for '-' and exits 1.
with_strategy: wordcount prints one stderr line naming <stdin>, nothing on stdout, no traceback, and exits 1.

walkthrough.name: No argument
today: It prints usage to stderr and exits 2.
with_strategy: It still prints usage to stderr and exits 2, without reading stdin.
